title: Knowledge Check 10 - Lessons 46-50
description: Questions pooled from Lessons 46-50 - Data Mappers. Pass with 80% or higher to move toward unlocking the cert prep exam.

questions.question: A mapping must combine a first name and last name into a single full name field. What is the correct approach?
options: Use a string function to concatenate the two fields
Use a date function on the name
questions.explanation: A string concatenation function combines the two fields into one. Copying one field loses data, storing separately does not combine, and a date function is irrelevant to names.

questions.question: A source sends a date in one format and the target requires another. How should the mapping handle it?
options: Use a date function to convert the format
questions.explanation: A date function converts the format to what the target expects. Passing it through keeps the wrong format, and rejecting or storing raw does not convert it.

questions.question: A field must show one value when a condition is true and another when it is false. What should the mapping use?
questions.explanation: Conditional logic in a formula branches on the condition to return the correct value. String and date functions do not branch, and a direct copy ignores the condition.

questions.question: A Data Mapper reads a large dataset but only a few records are needed. What is the most effective performance optimization?
options: Filter in the SOQL WHERE clause
Read all records and discard extras
Use a Load instead of an Extract
questions.explanation: Filtering in the WHERE clause reduces the data read at the database. Output filtering still pulls the full dataset, and the other options do not reduce the read.

questions.question: A Data Mapper returns every field on an object but the mapping uses only three fields. What should the consultant do?
options: Select only the three fields used
questions.explanation: Selecting only the needed fields reduces payload size and processing time. Returning all fields wastes resources, and the other options do not address the field selection.

questions.question: Two Data Mappers in a flow read the same records. What is the best performance improvement?
options: Reuse the data from the first read instead of re-querying
questions.explanation: Reusing data already in context eliminates the duplicate read. Keeping both reads wastes resources, and the other options do not remove the redundancy.

questions.question: A Data Mapper must read a parent record and its related child records. What is the most efficient approach?
options: Query the parent, then query each child separately
Use a relationship query that traverses the relationship in one call
Use a Load to read the data
questions.explanation: A relationship query reads the parent and children together in one call, reducing the number of queries. Separate queries add reads, a Load writes, and querying only children misses the parent.

questions.question: A consultant needs to read data across related objects. Which Data Mapper type supports the relationship traversal?
questions.explanation: Extract supports the full SOQL feature set including relationship traversal. Turbo Extract has a narrower feature set, Load writes, and Transform does not query.

questions.question: The same reference data is needed multiple times in a flow and changes rarely. What is the best optimization?
options: Cache the result of the first read and reuse it
Use a Load to store it
questions.explanation: Caching the first read lets later steps reuse the data instead of re-querying. Re-querying repeats the cost, and the other options do not avoid the repeated read.

questions.question: A Load must create new records in Salesforce. What does the incoming data need?
options: The required fields for the object
A lookup to an existing record
questions.explanation: An insert creates new records and needs the required fields; Salesforce assigns the IDs. A record ID is for updates, an external ID is for upsert, and a lookup is not needed for a pure insert.

questions.question: A Load must update existing records and the incoming data does not carry the Salesforce record ID. What must the consultant do?
options: Resolve the target record through a lookup
questions.explanation: An update must resolve the target record, and a lookup does that when the ID is absent. Inserting creates duplicates, skipping loses the update, and a Transform does not write.

questions.question: A Load uses upsert to keep external data in sync with Salesforce. What determines whether a record is inserted or updated?
options: The value of the external ID key field
questions.explanation: Upsert uses the external ID key to decide: a matching key updates, a new key inserts. The record ID, order, and field count do not drive the upsert decision.

questions.question: A Load processes many records and some fail validation. What should the flow do?
options: Handle the failures while keeping the successful writes
questions.explanation: A Load can succeed on some records and fail on others, so the flow should handle the failures without discarding the successes. Aborting loses good writes, and ignoring or re-running does not fix the failures.

questions.question: A consultant wants to catch bad records before they reach the Load. What is the best approach?
options: Let the Load fail and report
Validate the data before the write
Use a Transform after the Load
questions.explanation: Validating before the Load catches missing required fields and invalid values early. Letting the Load fail is reactive, skipping validation invites errors, and a Transform after the Load does not prevent the write failure.

questions.question: An upsert fails because the key field matches multiple records. What is the most likely cause?
options: The key field is not unique
questions.explanation: An upsert key that matches multiple records means the key field is not unique, which breaks the upsert logic. The other options do not describe a duplicate-key failure.
